 Oral Judgment
Heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellant and the learned counsel appearing for the respondents.
2. The appellant's land bearing Sy.No.34/1 measuring 7 guntas in Mundagodu Village, Kasaba Hobli, Arkalgudu Taluk was acquired under the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
The preliminary notification was issued on 03.09.2009.
The Land Acquisition Officer granted a compensation of Rs.49,000/- per acre.
On reference, the Reference Court awarded Rs.25,000 per gunta.
On appeal being filed by the land loser, the Appellate Court awarded Rs.35,000 per gunta as the market value.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant/land loser would submit that, in respect of the land acquired under the same notification in the same village and which is NC: 2026:KHC:6788 HC-KAR similar to the land of the appellant, compensation of Rs.45,000 per gunta is awarded by this Court in M.S.A. No.25/2023.

4. Learned counsel for the respondent does not dispute the fact that Rs.45,000 per gunta is awarded by this Court in M.S.A. No.25/2023 and does not dispute the fact that there is no appeal filed against the said order.
However, he would urge that the compensation awarded to the appellant is adequate and there is no scope for enhancement.
5. The Court has considered the contentions raised at the bar and perused the records.

6. In M.S.A. No.25/2023, the Court was dealing with the question relating to the market value in respect to the land acquired under the preliminary notification dated 03.09.2009 wherein the land acquired is of the same village and the purpose of acquisition was also same.
There appears to be no dispute that the land bearing Sy.No.34/1 and Sy.No.79/2 are in the close vicinity.

No NC:
2026:KHC:6788 HC-KAR material is placed on record to show that the land in question in the present appeal is inferior to the land bearing Sy.No.79/2 which was the subject matter of appeal in M.S.A. No.25/2023.

sentences.text: Under these circumstances, the Court is of the view that appellant is entitled to same higher compensation as awarded in MSA No.25/2023 and market share of the appellant's land is determined at Rs.45,000 per gunta with all other consequential benefits.

However, as already ordered on the interim application for condonation of delay, appellant is not entitled to interest on enhanced compensation for 994 days, in view of the delay in filing the appeal.
8. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed-in-part with proportionate costs.

Sd/-
